title: Taze Configuration
description: Configuration for taze. Used by .tazerc, .tazerc.json, and taze.config.{js,ts,mjs,cjs}.

$schema.description: JSON Schema reference for editor autocomplete and validation.

cwd.description: Working directory used to resolve packages.

recursive.description: Recursively search for supported files in subdirectories.

ignorePaths.description: Glob patterns to ignore when searching for supported files.

ignoreOtherWorkspaces.description: Ignore files in other workspaces (those with their own .git, pnpm-workspace.yaml, etc.).

include.description: Only the included dependencies will be checked for updates. Accepts a single pattern or a list.

exclude.description: Dependencies to exclude from the check. Overrides `include`. Accepts `name@range` (e.g. `typescript@7`) to exclude only matching versions instead of the whole package.

failOnOutdated.description: Exit with code 1 if outdated dependencies are found.

silent.description: Disable all output. Equivalent to setting `loglevel` to `"silent"`.

force.description: Force fetching from the registry, bypassing the cache.

peer.description: Include peerDependencies in the update process.

depFields.description: Fields in package.json to be checked. By default all fields are checked.

packageMode.description: Override bumping mode for specific dependencies. Keys are package names; values are the mode to use (or `"ignore"` to skip).

colors.description:
Optional color overrides for individual parts of taze's terminal output.

Keys describe where a color is used. Unspecified entries retain the original appearance from `DEFAULT_COLORS`; changing one role does not recolor other roles that happen to share the same default color.

Values accept ANSI color names, `#RGB` / `#RRGGBB` hex colors, or `false`. `false` applies no color at that role and can inherit a surrounding color. Existing bold, dim, inverse, and strikethrough styles remain in effect. Entries ending in `Bg` control backgrounds; the others control foregrounds. Terminal color support and `NO_COLOR` still apply.

In interactive lists, the focused row (`❯`) and checked dependencies (`◉`) are separate states. `interactiveSelectedBg` follows focus and defaults to `false`, preserving the original background.

packageName.description: Foreground color of the project/package name at the start of a package summary. Also used by the per-package up-to-date view. Dependency names in the table use `dependencyName`; package progress bars use `progressPackage`.

catalogName.description: Foreground color of the catalog name in a catalog header. For `pnpm-catalog:default`, this colors `default`; the `pnpm-catalog:` prefix keeps its dim style. Applies to pnpm, Bun, and Yarn catalogs.

dependencyName.description: Foreground color of a dependency name when its update is active. In interactive mode, active means checked for updating, independently of which row has keyboard focus. Inactive names use `dependencyUnselected`; active names with downgraded provenance use `provenanceWarningBg`.

dependencyAlias.description: Foreground color of the dim alias prefix before the underlying dependency name. For an aliased dependency displayed as `alias-name ← actual-name`, this colors `alias-name ← `. The prefix remains dim when a color is configured; `false` leaves it without its own foreground color.

dependencyGroup.description: Foreground color of dependency section headings when `group` is enabled. Examples include `dependencies`, `devDependencies`, and `peerDependencies`. The abbreviated source column in ungrouped output uses `dependencyType`.

dependencyType.description: Foreground color of the abbreviated dependency source column when `group` is false. Examples include `dev`, `peer`, and `optional`. Grouped output instead shows section headings colored by `dependencyGroup`.

dependencyUnselected.description: Foreground color of the name and target version of a dependency whose update is inactive. Used for unchecked rows in interactive mode and non-updating rows shown by `all`. The inactive target version retains its strikethrough style; the current-version column still uses `versionCurrent`.

packagePathMarker.description: Foreground color of the `›` marker in the header of a package with no name. The marker precedes the relative manifest path, such as `› package.json`. The path itself retains its dim style.

packageManager.description: Foreground color of `npm` or `pnpm` in a global-package summary header. The adjacent `(global)` label and installation path use `globalPackageInfo`. Progress bar labels for global packages use `progressDependency`.

globalPackageInfo.description: Foreground color of the extra information in global-package summary headers. Applies to the `(global)` label and, for pnpm, the global installation path. These pieces keep their dim style; the manager name uses `packageManager`.

upToDate.description: Foreground color of the per-package `✓ up to date` line when that view is rendered. This is the status inside an individual package's output when `all` is enabled. The overall `dependencies are already up-to-date` message uses `messageSuccess`.

versionCurrent.description: Foreground color of the current declared version on the left of an update. For example, colors `^1.0.0` in `^1.0.0 → ^2.0.0`. Also applies to the current-version column in the version selection list.

versionMajor.description: Foreground color of changed version digits for a major update and its numeric summary count. Version highlighting starts at the first differing segment: `1.2.3 → 2.0.0` colors `2.0.0`. The leading range prefix is controlled separately by `versionRange` and `versionRangeChanged`.

versionMinor.description: Foreground color of changed version digits for a minor update and its numeric summary count. For `1.2.3 → 1.3.0`, the highlighted portion is `3.0`. Shared leading version segments keep their existing uncolored appearance.

versionPatch.description: Foreground color of changed version digits for a patch update and its numeric summary count. For `1.2.3 → 1.2.4`, the highlighted portion is `4`. Also used as the fallback version-difference color when no diff type is available.

versionPin.description: Foreground color of a pinned target version or shortened GitHub Action commit SHA. Also colors the numeric `pin` count in the package summary. A trailing version annotation such as `# v4.2.0` keeps its dim style.

versionError.description: Foreground color of the numeric error count in a package's version-change summary. Used when a dependency's diff classification is `error`. Dependency resolution error text and the ERROR badge use `messageError`.

versionRange.description: Foreground color of an unchanged leading `^` or `~` in the target version. Also used for that prefix when range-prefix highlighting is disabled. The version digits are styled independently according to the version diff type.

versionRangeChanged.description: Foreground color of a target version's leading `^` or `~` when the range prefix changes. For `^1.0.0 → ~2.0.0`, this colors the new `~`. Applies when range-prefix highlighting is enabled; unchanged prefixes use `versionRange`.

versionAvailable.description: Foreground color of the dim `(x.y.z available)` notice after a dependency row. Shown when a newer available version differs from the chosen target version. The notice retains its dim style, independently of the target version's diff color.

versionArrow.description: Foreground color of the dim `→` between current and target versions. Used in dependency rows and the version selection list. The arrow between provenance status labels uses `provenanceArrow`.

nodeCompatible.description: Foreground color of a dependency's Node.js engine range when it is compatible. Shown when Node.js compatibility information is available and `nodecompat` is enabled. The range remains dim. The default `false` adds no foreground color.

nodeIncompatible.description: Foreground color of a dependency's Node.js engine range when it is incompatible with the current Node.js version. Shown when compatibility information is available and `nodecompat` is enabled; compatible ranges use `nodeCompatible`.

releaseAgeUnderHour.description: Foreground color of the `<1h` release-age label for elapsed times below one hour. Release ages describe time since publication, rather than calendar dates. Applies to both current and target release ages when `timediff` is enabled and the registry provides the corresponding publication timestamp.

releaseAgeHours.description: Foreground color of release ages from one hour up to, but excluding, 100 hours. The elapsed time is rounded to whole hours and displayed as `~24h`. Applies to both current and target releases; ages of 100 hours or more move to `releaseAgeDays`, even though a rounded hours label can reach `~100h`.

releaseAgeDays.description: Foreground color of release ages from 100 hours up to, but excluding, 30 days. The elapsed time is rounded to whole days and displayed as `~7d`. Applies to both current and target release-age columns when `timediff` is enabled.

releaseAgeMonths.description: Foreground color of release ages from 30 days up to, but excluding, 365 days. Each month is treated as 30 days; the result is rounded and displayed as `~3mo`. Applies to both release-age columns. This is independent of version-change colors, so changing it does not recolor major/minor/patch updates.

releaseAgeYears.description: Foreground color of release ages of 365 days or more, such as `~1.5y`. Each year is treated as 365 days, and the value is rounded to one decimal place with a trailing `.0` omitted. Applies to both release-age columns.

interactivePointer.description: Foreground color of the `❯` pointer identifying the row with keyboard focus. Used in both the dependency list and the version selection list. Focus moves with the navigation keys; checked state is indicated separately by `interactiveChecked` and `interactiveUnchecked`.

interactiveChecked.description: Foreground color of the `◉` marker for a dependency checked for updating. A checked dependency can be on any row, independently of keyboard focus. This option colors the marker; the dependency name uses `dependencyName`.

interactiveUnchecked.description: Foreground color of the `◌` marker for a dependency not checked for updating. The unchecked dependency's name and target version use `dependencyUnselected`. The focused row is identified independently by `interactivePointer`.

interactiveHint.description: Foreground color of the keyboard help text above the dependency list and the `Select a version for ... (current ...)` heading in version selection. Highlighted key names and the dependency name within these lines use `interactiveKey` and `interactiveDependencyName`, respectively.

interactiveKey.description: Foreground color of key names emphasized in the interactive keyboard help. Examples include `↑↓`, `space`, `enter`, `esc`, and `a`. The key names remain bold; the surrounding explanation uses `interactiveHint`.

interactiveBorder.description: Foreground color of the `┃` border beside interactive help and version headings. The border retains its bold and dim styles. Applies to both the dependency selection screen and the version selection screen.

interactiveDependencyName.description: Foreground color of the dependency name in the version selection heading. For `Select a version for vue (current ^3.0.0)`, this colors `vue`. The name remains bold; dependency names in the main table use `dependencyName`.

interactiveVersionName.description: Foreground color of an unfocused version category or tag in version selection. Examples include `minor`, `patch`, `latest`, and `next` when offered. The category on the focused row retains its existing uncolored appearance; the pointer and row background have their own interactive color options.

interactiveEndMarker.description: Foreground color of the `-- END --` marker appended to a long dependency list. The marker is added when the content reaches the terminal's available height and becomes visible as the rendered slice reaches the end of the list.

interactiveSelectedBg.description:
Background color of the row with keyboard focus in dependency or version selection. Tracks the `❯` pointer independently of whether the dependency is checked. The existing foreground colors and text styles are preserved; a specific cell background such as `provenanceWarningBg` can still appear within the row.

`false` leaves the terminal background in place. Set a color explicitly to enable highlighting, for example `'#333'` on a dark terminal or `'#eee'` on a light terminal. Applied to interactive TTY output when terminal colors are enabled.

provenanceCurrent.description: Foreground color of the current release's provenance status in a downgrade notice. Labels such as `trusted`, `provenance`, or `untrusted` remain bold. This is the status before the `provenanceArrow` in the dependency row.

provenanceTarget.description: Foreground color of the target release's provenance status in a downgrade notice. The bold label appears after `provenanceArrow`, for example `untrusted` in a change from `trusted → untrusted`.

provenanceArrow.description: Foreground color of the dim `→` between current and target provenance labels. Displayed for a dependency whose provenance has been downgraded. The version-change arrow is controlled independently by `versionArrow`.

provenanceWarning.description: Foreground color of the provenance downgrade warning paragraph below a package's table. Rendered when the displayed dependencies include a provenance downgrade. The paragraph remains bold; row status labels and the dependency-name background use the other `provenance*` color options.

provenanceWarningBg.description: Background color behind the name of an actively updated dependency with downgraded provenance. In interactive mode this warning background appears when that update is checked. Unchecked names use `dependencyUnselected`. This background stays visible within a focused row even when `interactiveSelectedBg` is enabled.

messageSuccess.description: Foreground color of overall success and up-to-date messages printed by the check command. Examples include `dependencies are already up-to-date` and summaries of packages already up to date. The individual `✓ up to date` line uses `upToDate`.

messageWarning.description: Foreground color of written-file notices and installation reminders. Examples include `ℹ changes written to package.json` and the reminder to install updated dependencies. Embedded commands use `hintCommand`.

messageError.description: Foreground color of dependency resolution error text and the `ERROR` badge. Examples include `package-name not found` and details of an unknown resolution error. The badge retains its inverse and bold styles, so this color appears as the badge background when inverse rendering swaps foreground and background.

operationStatus.description: Foreground color of taze's `installing...` and `updating...` status lines. These messages are printed immediately before invoking the package manager. Applies to local updates and, for installation, global package updates.

hintCommand.description: Foreground color of complete command snippets in usage hints and installation reminders. Examples include `taze major` and `pnpm i`. The surrounding message keeps its own color; individual suggested flags or mode arguments use `hintArgument`.

hintArgument.description: Foreground color of individual flags or mode arguments suggested by usage hints. Examples include `-w`, `-i`, and the standalone `major` mode in global-update hints. Complete suggested commands are colored by `hintCommand`.

promptMessage.description: Foreground color of the question text in write/install confirmation prompts. Examples include `write to package.json` and `install now`. Applies to the question supplied by taze; the prompt library handles its own input controls and answer indicators.

progressPackage.description: Foreground color of the package progress bar's `pkg` label and current package name. The package progress bar is created for recursive checks when packages are found. Dependency progress bars use `progressDependency` for their labels.

progressDependency.description: Foreground color of the dependency progress bar label. The label is `dep` for local checks and the package manager name, such as `npm` or `pnpm`, for global checks. The dependency name uses `progressName`.

progressName.description: Foreground color applied to the `{name}` placeholder in progress bar output. This normally displays the dependency currently being resolved. Package progress bar names carry their own `progressPackage` color inside this placeholder, which preserves the package-name emphasis.

update.description: Run the package manager's update command after bumping.

all.description: Show all packages, including those that are up to date.

json.description: Output update info as JSON to stdout. When enabled, `interactive` is ignored and no progress bars, tables, or tips are printed.

sort.description: Sort order for dependencies in the output.

group.description: Group dependencies by source (dependencies, devDependencies, etc.) on display.

timediff.description: Show time difference between the current and the updated version.

nodecompat.description: Show package compatibility with the current Node.js version.

maturityPeriod.description: Wait period in days before upgrading to newly released packages. Helps avoid potentially malicious packages released recently.

maturityPeriodExclude.description: Dependencies to exclude from the maturity period filter. Accepts a single pattern or a list.

concurrency.description: Number of concurrent requests when resolving dependencies.

requestTimeout.description: Request timeout in milliseconds when fetching package metadata.

githubActions.description: Check and update GitHub Actions referenced in .github/workflows/*.yml and composite action.yml files. Auto-enabled when a .github/workflows directory exists. Set to false to opt out, or pass an object to configure the behavior.

style.description: How to write updated `uses:` references. 'auto' preserves each action's existing style (tags stay tags, SHA pins stay SHA pins with a refreshed # vX.Y.Z comment), 'tag' always writes a tag reference, 'sha' always pins to a commit SHA with a version comment.

nodeVersion.description: Check and update the Node.js version declared in .node-version and .nvmrc files. Set to false to opt out.
